floor_history.headline: Recon: floor 17 is PURE register-rename — build emits all 170 insns in target's exact order; gap is exactly two allocation ties ($t1/$t2 and $v1/$a1); three ordering/spelling levers killed with measur

cc1 -da allocation dump turned this into a solvable simulation: loop1's ENTIRE register seating now equals target, s1's 'v1 must stay shared' constraint is overturned, and the whole residual is confin

frontier.hypothesis: The last half of tie B: inside loop2 the stored value must out-prioritise the walking pointer, so that the order becomes p, val, a0, ptr, w, r and each takes the lowest free register 2,3,4,5,6,7.
frontier.mechanism: 'val' has only 2 references ('val = w;' and '*p = val;') against 'ptr's 4-8, and both are tight-ranged, so floor_log2(2)*2/len loses badly to floor_log2(4)*4/len and ptr is allocated 4th in the whole function while val is second-to-last. This is the same inversion loop1 had, but loop1's fix (delete the conflict by splitting) is unavailable because val and ptr are genuinely both live across the inner loop.
frontier.next_probe: Attack ptr's live_length rather than val's ref count - ptr is defined immediately before loop2 so its range is only ~8 insns; try forms that legitimately lengthen it (e.g. deriving loop2's row base from a cursor the D_800EF0xx init block above already needs, if the semantics support it), and forms that give val a genuine third reference from surrounding code. Screen every form on the .greg dump with VSET=variantsN python3 sweep.py BEFORE scoring - the score alone hid the loop1 solution for an entire session.

frontier.hypothesis: Tie A needs a reference-count change that no structural lever can supply, so it belongs to a rederive/forensics session that re-expresses the two if/else arms.
frontier.mechanism: t1val 2 refs vs t2 3 refs at identical live ranges. If the counts were equal the tie breaks on allocno number and t1val (76) beats t2 (83), which is exactly target's seating. The arms' payloads are {s3val, t2, s1val, -0xC1, -0x100, -0x3FC1, -0x4000} and {s2val, t2, t1val, -0x40C1, -0x4100, -0x7FC1, -0x8000}: the SECOND element is t2 in both and the negative constants differ by exactly 0x4000 between arms.
frontier.next_probe: Re-express the arms from the primitive layout (tpage, clut, uv pairs; the 0x4000 arm delta looks like a semi-transparency/tpage bit) rather than as two duplicated literal store runs, and re-read the .greg dump for the t1val/t2 dispositions.

frontier.hypothesis: The candidate's dependence on the exact order 't2 = 0x2C00; a3 = 0; a0 = 0;' should be made non-arbitrary before it is ever put in front of the Judge.
frontier.mechanism: Pure allocno_live_length: a3 (6 refs) out-ranks t0 (5 refs) only while a3's live range is short, and each statement placed between 'a3 = 0;' and the loop head lengthens it. Not a coercion, but unmotivated as written.
frontier.next_probe: Find a natural loop shape giving the row counter the same live range - but a full nested for() rewrite of loop1 was measured to create two extra induction pseudos (t2 -> $t4, t1val -> $t3), so re-read the dump after any loop-shape change rather than assuming shape neutrality.
